reading.body:
QTS Santa Clara 1 publishes 7.5 MW of critical power, enough to support roughly 187 racks at AI training density or 750 racks at colocation density, though these are assumptions about rack utilization not operator claims.

The facility holds LEED Silver certification but publishes no Tier classification, SOC attestation, or federal compliance credential. This means workloads requiring those certifications cannot be verified against this data. Within California, it ranks fourth by published capacity among seven facilities that disclose megawatt figures at all, holding roughly 4 percent of the 185 MW total across those seven sites. California's documented grid constraints affect all facilities in the state, but no power availability or utility capacity data is published for this campus specifically.

At 7.5 MW, Santa Clara 1 is a mid-small facility in a dense market. It is meaningful for regional colocation but lacks the scale for large-scale AI training on capacity alone. The operator's rebrand from QTS to Q since the last data update reflects the sector's consolidation, common among mid-tier datacenter operators.
